html:
A religion that joins Native American beliefs with parts of Christianity, and uses the peyote cactus as a sacrament. It was incorporated as a church in Oklahoma in 1918 and is now the most widespread Indigenous religion in the United States.

Peyote, a small cactus that causes visions, had been used in ritual for thousands of years in northern Mexico. In the late 1800s, on the reservations of Indian Territory, the Comanche leader Quanah Parker and others spread a new ceremony: an all night meeting of prayer, song and drumming around a fire, in which peyote is eaten to bring people closer to the Creator. It offered healing and a way to stay sober and keep Native identity, at a time when the US government was suppressing traditional religions. Like the Ghost Dance, it spread between many peoples.

Members incorporated the church to defend their practice in law. Courts and laws went back and forth; a 1994 federal law finally protected the religious use of peyote by Native Americans.
sum: A religion that joins Native American beliefs with parts of Christianity, and uses the peyote cactus as a sacrament. It was incorporated as a church in Oklahoma in 1918 and is now the most widespread Indigenous religion in the United States…
